demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- India's Digital media segment is projected to grow at a CAGR of 14% from CY 2025 to CY 2028E, reaching approximately INR 1.64 trillion, supported by continued expansion in Digital advertising, increasing subscription adoption, deeper regional language penetration, and ongoing digital transformation of consumer and advertiser behaviour.
- Digital advertising is projected to grow at a 14% CAGR to reach approximately INR 1,393 billion by CY 2028E, driven by continued growth in digital consumption, expanding e-commerce ecosystems, increasing adoption of programmatic technologies, and deeper penetration among SMEs.
- The online news segment continues to face monetization challenges despite maintaining a meaningful audience reach, with a modest decline in reach during the year attributed to increasing use of AI-powered search summaries and emerging AI applications affecting traffic patterns and content discovery.
- Growth in news (via app-led OTTs) advertising was relatively modest at 13% as AI-powered search summaries and content discovery tools reduced traffic to traditional news websites, while content saturation and heightened competition constrained audience growth.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- brand: livemint.com ranks among India's top business news websites in terms of audience engagement and continued to strengthen its position as one of India's most trusted and influential business and financial news platforms — evidence: Ranked No. 4 Business news site (based on Mar'26 page views as per ComScore)
- distribution: unified digital subscription platform spans hindustantimes.com, livehindustan.com and livemint.com, reinforcing the Company's position among India's leading paid news destinations — evidence: one of the top news publishers by paid subscriber base
- customer lock-in: proprietary customer data platform (CDP) provides advertisers cohort-based demographic and interest-based targeting — evidence: CDP was further enhanced during the year, per the MD&A

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company's risk identification exercise flags high dependence on digital platforms as a risk affecting the business.
- Growing use of AI-enabled discovery and conversational tools is flagged as a risk that could affect traffic and audience reach for the Company's news platforms.
- The Company flags the rapid growth of AI-driven content, together with evolving copyright and governance frameworks around it, as a risk and uncertainty affecting the business.
- The Company identifies challenges in managing cyber security and digital personal data handling as a business risk, addressed via MFA, EDR, CASB, DLP and a 24/7 SOC team.
- The Company flags rapid shifts in audience consumption patterns, content formats and delivery mediums as a risk to its digital media business.
